Loading instruction: step-by-step packing and pallet build for the warehouse team. Full specification: carton, pallet, strength, transit, freight and assumptions for quality, packaging, logistics and supply chain. Both use the carton and pallet option shown above.

How the numbers are made
  • Cartons are regular slotted cartons (RSC, FEFCO-ESBO code 0201) built around a block of units plus packing clearance. Side walls add 2 board thicknesses per dimension. The flap direction adds 4, because the flaps overlap 2 deep at the top and at the bottom. Every flap direction is tried.
  • Board thickness defaults sit at or above the nominal flute thickness published by the Fibre Box Association (F 0.8, E 1.6, B 3.2, C 4.0 mm) and the top of the DIN 55468 flute height ranges used in Europe, so cartons are never drawn undersized. Double and triple wall add each flute plus a liner. Ask your supplier for the measured thickness (ISO 3034) and edge crush (ISO 3037 or TAPPI T 811). ECT and board weight here are typical values.
  • Layers come from guillotine and 5-block pinwheel patterns. With brick wall on, every layer must bridge the joints below by the share you set, and every carton needs 75% of its base supported.
  • Compression uses the McKee short formula, BCT = 5.87 × ECT × √(thickness × perimeter), an industry estimate to be confirmed by a box compression test (ISO 12048 or ASTM D642). It is reduced when layers interlock and when a carton lies on its side. Required strength is the load above the carton times the safety factor.
  • Transit checks are theoretical. They map to ISTA 1A, 2A (single cartons up to 68 kg) and 1E, 3E (unit loads). Drop heights and test loads come from the full ISTA procedures, which are not public, so lab testing is still needed.
